2. The case of the petitioner, in short, is that the petitioner instituted a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of suit land in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Fulpur, Mymensingh being the Other Suit No. 121 of 1999 in respect of 14½ steaks of land out of 58 sataks in RS plot No. 241 under RS khatian No. 125 corresponding to CS khatian No. 55 in Mouza 55 Rampur, District Mymensingh stating that he got 7½ sataks of land from one Hamida under a Gift Deed No. 5190 dated 8-4-1991 and another 7½ sataks of land under an Ewaj Deed (exchange) No. 5573 dated 4-5-1991 with Salam, Fazlu and Nurunnahar and while in possession of the said land by growing paddy and making dwelling hut, was forcibly dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants on 9-6-1991. 

 4. The learned trial Court has been pleased to dismiss the suit on his findings that the Exhibit-Ka i.e. RoR Khatian was prepared and recorded in the names of Korban Ali and Hatem Ali, instead of Abdul Jabbar's daughters Hamida and Sajeda, predecessors of the plaintiff in respect of 28 sataks of land which they had allegedly inherited from their father and though the plaintiff claimed that in a family arrangements Hamida and Sajeda got 14½ sataks of land and Korban Ali got 13½ sataks out of the schedule property, but the plaintiff could not produce any deed of family arrangements. The plaintiffs statements that Hamida transferred 7½ sataks of land to him under a Heba Deed No. 5190 dated 8-4-1991 and another 7½ sataks from Sajeda's children by way of exchange could not be accepted in the absence of authentic deed of family arrangements and also in view of the fact that the RoR khatian was not recorded in the names of the predecessors of the plaintiff. The plaintiff could not adduce any reliable evidence in support of the alleged gift and he also failed to provide any reasonable circumstances in support of the alleged exchange. It appeared to the learned trial Court that the defendant did not dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land. 

 16. PW 1 stated in his evidence that the CS khatian No. 55, in respect of the suit property, stood recorded in the names of Nabijan Bibi, Hatem Ali Tarafdar, Nurjahan Bibi, Abdul Jabbar and Abdul Latif in their respective shares, (Exhibit 1). There was a family settlement about the suit land among Nabijan Bibi and others and in that arrangements, Abdul Jabbar got 28 sataks of land and died leaving behind two daughters, Hamida and Sajeda and two sons Korban Ali and Hatem Ali Tarafder. The RoR khatian No. 125 was recorded in the name of Hatem Ali and Korban Ali Tarafdar, sons of Abdul Jabbar Exhibit 1 (ka) leaving aside two daughters. After death of Abdul Jabbar Tarafdar the property was divided among his two sons and two daughters under a family arrangements and under the said family arrangements, daughter Hamida got 7 sataks in the plot No. 241 and Sajeda got 7½ sataks in plot No. 241. Korban Ali got 13½ sataks. Hatem Ali got in other plots. In CS khatian No. 55 there were total 5.67 acres of land under 12 plots. Hamida Khatoon has gifted her 7 sataks land to the plaintiff by a registered Ewaj deed dated 8-4-1991 (Exhibit 2) and gave him possession therein and the heirs of Sajeda Khatoon have exchanged that 7½ sataks of land which their mother had inherited, with the plaintiff under a registered Ewaj deed No. 5573 dated 4-5-1999 (Exhibit 3) and thereby, heis in possession of total 13-1/2) sataks of land in CS plot No. 241 under the CS khatian No. 55. 

 18. The appellate Court has made a passing remark that the deeds of the plaintiff are not disputed and the trial Court has ventured to surmises and conjectures, why on earth Hamida would made a gift in favour of the plaintiff who is not a direct descendent of her brother while her brother had children of his own to have the gift and why Sajeda should exchange part of the suit land, etc. None of the Courts below found that those deeds of plaintiff were not genuine, not acted upon or not proved by evidence. Exhibit 4 is the family Bantannama being No. 5579 dated 4-5-1991 between Hamida Khatoon, Md Fazlul Hoque, Md Abdus Salam, Mosammat Tahurun Nessa, wife of late HatemAli showing that the property recorded in the CS plot No. 241 under CS khatian No. 55 measuring 14½ sataks in the share of the 1st party, Hamida Khatoon. But the learned trial Court has opined that in the absence of an authentic family Bantannama, plaintiffs predecessor's title and possession could not be held. This Court did not discuss anything as to how this registered deed, the Exhibit 4, was not authentic in the absence of any evidence to the contrary or of rebuttal. Without assessing the evidence on record this Court has opined that the plaintiff could not adduce reliable evidence. Both in the plaint and evidence, PW 1 has categorically stated the boundary of the disputed land together with its neighbours by contiguity identifying the same distinctly and separately, but still the learned appellate Court found that a suit for declaration of title with recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in a joint jote in utter disregard of categorical documentary and oral evidence that the CS plot No. 241 was separately identifiable. None of these two Courts however, followed the issues suggested by the appellate Court in Other Appeal No. 143 of 1996 in terms in the courts of their discussions, findings.
